verdict: Williams-Sonoma grew sales 6.7% to $2.0B with every brand up, though a $168M tariff refund — not store trading — explains most of the jump in GAAP profit.

kpis.label: Comparable brand revenue
kpis.note: growth at established stores and online, vs a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (non-GAAP)
kpis.note: excludes the IEEPA tariff refund and related items

segments.name: Pottery Barn
segments.note: Furniture and home furnishings under the Pottery Barn brand — the largest brand in the group.

segments.name: West Elm
segments.note: Modern furniture and decor aimed at younger, urban customers.

segments.name: Williams Sonoma
segments.note: Kitchen and cooking brands, including Williams Sonoma Home.

segments.name: Pottery Barn Kids and Teen
segments.note: Children's and teens' furniture and decor (rounded up $1M so brand figures sum to total net revenues).

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Rejuvenation, Mark and Graham, GreenRow, Dormify and international franchise operations — the fastest-growing group this quarter.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Store, head-office, employment and advertising costs — 28.7% of revenue on a GAAP basis, including a one-time $10M tariff-related employee recognition contribution.

otherDetail: Interest income, net of $12M — including $6M of interest received alongside the IEEPA tariff refunds.
oneTimers: GAAP results include IEEPA tariff refunds: a $168M reduction in cost of goods sold plus $6M of interest income, partly offset by a $48M provision to reimburse vendors for tariff concessions and a $10M one-time employee recognition contribution. Excluding these, operating income was $338M and EPS was $2.10 (non-GAAP).
A further $29M of tariff refund income was deferred inside merchandise inventories at quarter-end and is expected to reduce cost of goods sold in the next quarter.

takeaways.title: Every brand grew
takeaways.text: Comparable brand revenue rose 6.2% and total revenue 6.7%, with Pottery Barn, West Elm, Williams Sonoma and Pottery Barn Kids and Teen all up — and management raised full-year guidance.

takeaways.title: A refund flatters GAAP profit
takeaways.text: The $168M IEEPA tariff refund cut cost of goods sold and lifted the GAAP gross margin to 51.6%; without the tariff items the gross margin was 45.5%, down on last year as tariff costs bit into merchandise margins.

takeaways.title: Cash pile intact
takeaways.text: Williams-Sonoma held $1.0B of cash, generated $696M of operating cash flow in the half (including collecting the tariff refunds) and kept inventories nearly flat, up just 1.0% year on year.

footerNote: Williams-Sonoma reports cost of goods sold including occupancy costs (store rent and related costs sit in cost of goods sold, not in SG&A) — the chart follows that printed layout. This is the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (the fiscal year ending in early 2027), ended August 2, 2026. Figures are the Form 10-Q's printed amounts in $M; brand revenues in the 10-Q are in thousands and Pottery Barn Kids and Teen is rounded up $1M so the brands sum exactly to total net revenues.
